model.py and losses.py are copied unchanged.
ng.py has two compatibility/correctness changes:
- Clone node attributes before an in-place feature swap. DGL graph.clone()
  shares feature tensors; otherwise generation changes the normal reference.
- Construct the dense adjacency from edges with numpy.add.at instead of
  g.adj().to_dense(), avoiding DGL's optional version-specific sparse library.
  Parallel edges retain their multiplicity.

The adapter uses the released architecture, spectral/feature generator,
log-ratio objective, and Adam settings from configs/MUTAG.yaml. It uses the
local TU feature preprocessing, normal-only splits and minibatch sizes.
It trains fixed epochs, without the upstream trainer's test-metric checkpoint
selection. Scoring uses every training reference with exact weighted chunk
means, instead of the upstream trainer's final training batch only.
The default framework calibrates thresholds on held-out normals. Earlier
integration runs used training-normal scores; neither uses test scores.
These are common-protocol runs, not exact reproductions of the paper table.
CPU dependency compatibility was tested with DGL 1.1.3/PyTorch 2.5.1/Python 3.10;
the upstream README recommends a different, newer DGL/CUDA environment.

Performance integration: src/models/benchmarks/lgkde_distance.py subclasses DGMMD and
vectorizes its graph-pair kernel means via normalized membership matrices.
The official model.py remains byte-for-byte unchanged. Values and parameter
gradients are checked against official loops for both within-set and cross-set
MMD. Floating-point reduction order differs; numerical training trajectories
need not be bit-identical to the loop implementation.
